where: the notice at the top of Amara Whitfield's editor (x 468–972, y 92–320) and the 'Create her in Planning Center' button under it (x 484–956, y 275–307); Amara's row mark on both list frames (row 10, x 585–768)
finding: Three frames in the same round give Dana three different accounts of the one thing J6 is about — whether Amara's *link* is in flight — and the frame that asks her to act is the one that says both at once. sync-blocked tells her 'She was quick-added at the door 40 seconds ago and is still waiting to be created there', which is a job with an age and no work for her, and then puts an enabled 'Create her in Planning Center' button directly under it whose caption promises it 'unlocks these boxes in a few seconds'. If the create is already going out, pressing is at best redundant; if it is not, not pressing means a child recorded at the door never reaches the church database. Dana cannot tell which from the frame, and the operation she is being asked to guess about is the one the brief names as the failure mode this codebase is most careful about. Meanwhile the list she surveys from files her in neither job pill: 'In flight 3' and 'Needs you 2' both exclude her, and her mark is neutral ink, so a pending or press-me create is the one job class no count on the screen can reach — the exact gap round 2 closed for `differs` and left open here.

If the create is queued like an edit, then it is a job: give it the queued mark with its age on both lists, count it in 'In flight', and take the Create button off sync-blocked (replace with 'Cancel this create', the same move the queued strip already offers). where: the differs strip's message and provenance lines (x 553–929, y 188–306, and the two-up cells at y 337–414); the orphaned strip's message and its 'Re-create her in Planning Center' button (x 528–848, y 371–403)
finding: Asked directly: the merged-upstream case does not need a scene of its own — its shape is exactly `differs` (it landed, and what came back is not what was sent, and there are two values and two moves). But it is not adequately covered as the frames stand, because `differs` narrates a cause that would be false and `orphaned` offers a move that would be dangerous. The differs copy hard-codes a single story — 'At 9:08 the church office changed the same field to Ito' — and repeats it as provenance under the live cell ('the church office · 9:08'). After a merge nobody changed that field; the edit landed on a different person under a different id, and the surname on the record is the survivor's. Dana is then shown two matched buttons and asked to choose, on a history the product invented, with no way to see whose record her value would go to if she presses 'Send Chen-Ito again'. The orphaned frame is worse as a fallback: if the merge trail is not followed the record reads as deleted, and the one loud move on that screen writes a new person into the church's permanent database — a duplicate of the survivor she was merged into.
evidence: grep across all eight sync prototypes: zero occurrences of merge/merged outside the word 'emergency'; the only 'Merged into' string in `uxr/prototype/` belongs to the review scene, a different journey. sync-differs strip: actor 'the church office', times 9:05/9:08/9:12, cells 'ON THE RECORD NOW / Ito / the church office · 9:08' and 'YOU TYPED / Chen-Ito / you · 9:05'. sync-orphaned strip: 'the person it names was deleted in Planning Center on 4 August', action 'Re-create her in Planning Center' with the guarantee 'It writes one new person and never a second copy' — a guarantee about duplicate *jobs*, not about a person who already exists under another id. JOURNEY-profile-sync.md lists merged-upstream first under 'Things about identity — the dangerous class'.
direction: One branch of the strip that already exists, not a ninth frame: when the drain followed a merge, the differs strip's actor becomes the merge rather than a person — 'This record was merged into <name> in Planning Center on Tuesday. Your correction landed there, not here' — the live cell's provenance line names the survivor and links to them, and the second action is 'Open <survivor>' instead of 'Send it again', because sending again into a record the leader has not seen is not a choice she can make informed. And `orphaned` should be able to say which of the two it is: deleted and re-creatable, or merged and not.
